title: 2026-11-17_Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_1d2
description: Security monitoring has detected unusual activity on the target system, potentially indicating the presence of the Sofacy Fysbis backdoor. Your task is to investigate this activity, identify the malicious components, and implement appropriate containment measures.
outcomes: Investigate suspicious services and network activity
Identify malicious components and their behavior
Implement containment measures to prevent further unauthorized access

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: System information appears to be collected automatically without an authorized administrative purpose. Investigate the host and identify the file responsible for this activity.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target system (192.168.50.5) via SSH using the provided credentials.
levels.local_content: Access the target system (192.168.50.5) via SSH using the provided credentials.

levels.title: Suspicious File Discovery
levels.content: System information appears to be collected automatically without an authorized administrative purpose. Investigate the host and identify the file responsible for this activity.
levels.solution:
1. List all systemd services to identify suspicious components:
   ```
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
   ```
2. Investigate the local-inventory.service, which appears to be responsible for collecting system information:
   ```
systemctl cat local-inventory.service
   ```
3. Identify the executable file responsible for the data collection:
   ```
systemctl show local-inventory.service -p ExecStart
   ```
4. The file /usr/local/bin/local-inventory.sh is responsible for collecting system information.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use systemctl commands to list and investigate services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The ExecStart property of a service unit file shows the command that is executed when the service starts.

levels.title: Data Exfiltration Detection
levels.content: Security monitoring suggests that information collected from the compromised host may be accessible to an unauthorized remote system. Investigate the available network and filesystem evidence to identify the affected data file and determine how it is exposed or transferred.
levels.solution:
1. List all active network connections to identify suspicious communication:
   ```
ss -tunap
   ```
2. Investigate the bkd.service, which appears to be responsible for network communication:
   ```
systemctl cat bkd.service
   ```
3. Check the journal logs for the bkd.service to understand its behavior:
   ```
journalctl -u bkd.service
   ```
4. The service is listening on port 80 and sending the contents of /var/log/local-inventory/inventory.log to connecting clients.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use ss command to list active network connections.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Investigate the service responsible for the suspicious network communication.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Check the journal logs for the service to understand its behavior.

levels.title: C2 Containment
levels.content: Investigation has identified unauthorized communication involving the compromised host. Apply an appropriate network control to prevent further communication with the suspicious remote system while preserving legitimate network access.
levels.solution:
1. Identify the IP address of the remote system communicating with the compromised host:
   ```
journalctl -u bkd.service | grep "connected from"
   ```
2. Block the remote IP address using iptables:
   ```
sudo iptables -I INPUT -s <remote_ip> -j DROP
   ```
3. Verify that the remote IP address is blocked:
   ```
sudo iptables -L -n -v
   ```
4. The remote IP address <remote_ip> is now blocked, preventing further unauthorized communication.
